newsitem.title: ITALY: At least five injured in Italy plane accident.
newsitem.headline: At least five injured in Italy plane accident.

text.p: At least five people were injured, one seriously, when a small airliner overshot a runway at Florence airport in Italy on Wednesday and stopped just short of a busy highway.

The Air Littoral ATR-42 turbo prop plane, on a flight from the French resort of Nice carrying 14 passengers and three crew, failed to stop at the end of the runway after landing at Florence airport, fire officials said.

It broke through a perimeter fence and ploughed on towards a motorway, its nose hitting the highway guard rail. Television footage showed parts of the 23-metre-long (74 foot) plane had been snapped off.
Firemen cut into the wreckage to free the pilots, one of whom was taken to hospital where doctors said he was in a serious condition. The passengers left the plane by a rear door.
A fire brigade spokesman in Rome said at least five passengers were hurt. A hostess was also on board.

Most of the injuries appeared to be minor, including bruises and cuts. Doctors said all 14 of the passengers had been taken to hospital for checks but most were expected to be released during the day.
The highway, a major east-west link which leads to Italy's Mediterranean coast, was closed and traffic and was backed up for several kilometres (miles).
Air Littoral, a French regional airline which is majority-owned by businessman Michel Seydoux, is based in Montpellier, France.
